title: Introduce CI Jigsaw presubmit splitter and dependency sweeper
author: Noah Patel
description:
Motivation: Presubmit latency and noisy failures were increasing due to a monolithic lint/test presubmit that runs all linters and language checks for every change. This PR introduces the CI Jigsaw: a presubmit decomposer that routes changes to language-aware lint/test runners, a lightweight fastpath lane for trivial changes, and a dependency sweeper that quarantines and annotates unstable transitive dep updates. Goals: reduce overall presubmit time for common edits, make CI failures more actionable by narrowing the runner surface, and surface dependency instability to a dedicated workflow instead of polluting presubmit runs.

Summary of changes: - Add a new presubmit router (ci/presubmit/jigsaw) that inspects changed files and selects a minimal set of runners (js/ts, python, go, infra, docs). - Split the existing monolithic lint job into language plugins and a thin orchestrator that composes jobs. - Introduce a "fastpath" presubmit lane for docs/changelog/README-only edits that completes in <30s. - Add dep-sweeper workflow (ci/dep-sweeper) that runs nightly, runs dependency upgrade candidates through a stability harness, and posts labels/comments on flaky candidates. - Add lightweight annotations to PR results that point to the responsible runner and flakiness score. - Update presubmit docs and badges.

Why this is different: instead of adding more shards, this PR changes presubmit selection semantics and moves noisy dependency validation out of blocking premerge checks. It also provides a clearer remediation path (re-run specific language runner) rather than re-running the entire matrix.

Checklist: - [x] Add presubmit router and language profiles - [x] Implement fastpath detection heuristics - [x] Add dep-sweeper workflow and reporting - [x] Add e2e smoke test for router selection - [x] Update CONTRIBUTING.md and docs/redwood-ci.md - [x] Run canary on infra team for two weeks

Testing and rollout plan: staged rollout. Canary on infra and SDK repos for 2 weeks; metric to monitor: median presubmit duration, flake rate, and false-negative selection (where router omits a needed runner). Feature gated via repo config: ci/presubmit/config.yaml. Reverted default behavior if regressions observed.

Related: Linear items ENG-2345, ENG-2897. See internal RFC: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2345/ci-jigsaw-presubmit-router (internal link).

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps language runner implementations small and backwards compatible. The old monolithic workflow is removed after successful canary and one-week global rollout. There are follow-up items to add telemetry for per-runner tokenized cost attribution and to add a presubmit dry-run mode for dependabot PRs.
commits: feat(ci): add presubmit router and selection heuristics
refactor(ci): decompose monolithic lint into language plugins
feat(ci): add fastpath lane for docs-only changes
feat(ci): introduce dep-sweeper nightly workflow and report
test(ci): add e2e smoke tests for router selection
docs: update contributing and CI docs
release_notes: Adds CI presubmit router that selects minimal language runners, introduces a fastpath for docs-only edits, and a nightly dependency sweeper that quarantines unstable upgrades. No user-facing changes. Rollout: canary then global.
review_comments: Maya Chen (2026-02-11): Can the fastpath detector be bypassed by a changed changelog plus a codegen file? Please add a deterministic allowlist check. -- addressed in a follow-up commit that adds filename allowlist and unit test.

Diego Alvarez (2026-02-12): dep-sweeper reports are great; can we surface the flakiness score as a label instead of comment? Suggestion: add 'dep-flaky' label for triage. -- author: added label workflow and documented expected triage steps.
Rina Sato (2026-02-14): e2e smoke sometimes times out in CI matrix; increase timeout for router lookup and add retry. -- addressed by increasing lookup timeout and retries.
Infra Team (2026-02-15): Canary run on infra repo showed median presubmit down 48% and flake rate reduced from 6.2% to 3.1%. Approved for wider rollout.
